forecasts.reason: The mechanism's clause that a cut sample casts no vote, so the score is bounded by finishable problems and not by vote size, applies here because min-p truncation brings loops and cap hits back (min-p 0.1 on MATH-500 took cap hits from 27 to 58); fewer finished votes put the route slightly under this shard's stored base vote of 22 of 41.

By the same cap-bound clause, RL rarely hits the cap (20 of 328), so min-p takes few votes away and RL stays near its stored vote rate; that rate is scaled down to about 26 of 41 because the base's shard figure (22 against a 24.0 average) shows this shard is harder than average.

The cap-bound clause gives a small loss on MATH-500: most problems finish well under the cap and right answers are short (median 1,432 tokens), so the few extra min-p cap hits cost about 1 point against the stored 89.2 of 100.
